body:
Arjun: Quick follow-up from last night's cross-region routing/DNS incident. Postmortem is live: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/inc-1762000123-routing-dns 
Arjun: TL;DR — asymmetric route preference + LB TLS cert chain mismatch in eu-west caused TCP resets. Clients retried to us-east, which amplified requests and triggered 5xx spikes.
Arjun: I pulled together remediation items below. Please ack, own, and put tentative due dates. We want a coordinated rollout with canary.

Maya: Ack. I can take the LB/TLS items.
Maya: Item 1: Enforce cert chain validation across region LB pools and add explicit SNI mapping so certs don't get rejected during cross-region failover. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-03-30. Ticket: ENG-5678.

Lia: I’ll own infra routing rule audit and automated tests.
Lia: Item 2: Audit regional route preferences and add a unit test that simulates regional failovers. Owner: Lia. Due: 2026-04-06. Ticket: TKT-3421.

Arjun: Item 3: Add prefix/KV cache guard to prevent retry amplification for downstream services (quick patch + longer-term throttling). Owner: Arjun + SRE. Due: quick patch 2026-03-28, rollout 2026-04-13. Ticket: MON-912.

Oliver: Customer impact question — any external-facing incidents reported?
Oliver: We should notify customers on the affected SLA page if rollouts change.

Arjun: No major data loss but increased latency for some API endpoints for ~47 minutes. Follow-up comms = customer success to draft; Oliver can coordinate.

Maya: Proposed LB healthcheck/config snippet to apply to eu-west pool (canary first):
```yaml
health_check:
  protocol: TLS
  verify_cert: true
  sni: "edge.redwood.com"
  fallback_policy: "reject_on_mismatch"
```
Maya: Will open PR against infra-config repo and ping for review.

Lia: On the routing tests: I'll add a synthetic that flips route preference to emulate partial BGP withdrawal and ensure we don't get asymmetric handoffs. Will post test plan by EOD.

Arjun: Recurrence notes: similar symptoms in 2025-11 and 2026-01 (see postmortems linked in doc). Pattern: cross-region TLS mismatches surface only under partial control-plane instability — so both LB config and stronger monitoring needed.

Maya: Suggest adding a composite alert that fires when (TLS handshake failures per-region > 0.5% AND retry rate > 2x baseline) for 5m. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-03-31. Alert ticket: MON-913.

oncall-bot: Created issues MON-912, ENG-5678, TKT-3421, MON-913 and assigned to listed owners. Next review meeting scheduled: 2026-04-06 10:00 UTC.

Oliver: Can we get a simple rollback playbook for the LB change in case canary shows regressions?
Maya: Yes — rollback is a single config flip and re-propagate. I'll add steps to the PR and the runbook.

Arjun: Outstanding:
- Maya: LB config PR + alert (ENG-5678, MON-913) — due 2026-03-30/31
- Lia: routing tests + audit (TKT-3421) — due 2026-04-06
- Arjun/SRE: cache guard quick patch (MON-912) — quick patch 2026-03-28
- Oliver: Customer comms draft and SLA page update — due 2026-03-31

Arjun: Anything else? If no objections, we'll treat these as action items from the postmortem and track in the weekly incident follow-up board. :white_check_mark:
